queries: WITH c AS (SELECT o.ordertune, COUNT(DISTINCT o.orderspivot) AS cnt FROM orders o JOIN riskandmargin r ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.ordertune), a AS (SELECT AVG(cnt) AS av FROM c) SELECT AVG(c.cnt) AS avg_count_above_avg, AVG(c.cnt - a.av) AS avg_excess_over_avg FROM c CROSS JOIN a WHERE c.cnt > a.av

assumptions.assumption: Each order is counted once per order type (distinct orders that have at least one matching risk/margin record), not once per risk/margin row.

The average across types is the unweighted mean of per-type counts, taken only over order types that have at least one matched order. Types with no matched orders are excluded. A NULL ordertype, if present, is treated as its own group.
'Above the average' means strictly greater than the mean. The excess is each type's count minus the unrounded mean.

alternatives.interpretation: Count matched risk/margin rows (join rows) per order type instead of distinct orders. This differs only if an order has multiple risk/margin records.
alternatives.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT o.ordertune, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM orders o JOIN riskandmargin r ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.ordertune), a AS (SELECT AVG(cnt) AS av FROM c) SELECT AVG(c.cnt) AS avg_count_above_avg, AVG(c.cnt - a.av) AS avg_excess_over_avg FROM c CROSS JOIN a WHERE c.cnt > a.av

assumptions.assumption: Each order is counted once per order type (distinct orders), even if several risk/margin records match it.
Orders with a NULL order type are not treated as a type and are excluded from the groups and the average.
Only types strictly above the average count are kept. If no type is above it (all counts equal), the query returns one row of NULLs.

alternatives.interpretation: Count matched risk/margin records (join rows) per order type instead of distinct orders.

assumptions.assumption: Each order is counted once per order type, using COUNT(DISTINCT recordvault), even if it has several risk/margin records.
The average across types is the unweighted mean of the per-type counts. 'Above average' means strictly greater than that mean. Averages are returned unrounded.
Any NULL ordertune is treated as its own group, since the request does not mention it.
